baslik: The Invisible Downdraft That Slammed a Jet Into the Ground
sonuc: crashed short of the runway at Dallas/Fort Worth
tetik: a microburst beneath a thunderstorm on final approach
mekanizma: microburst wind shear causing a sudden loss of airspeed and lift near the ground
ders: airports got Doppler wind-shear radar and jets got predictive wind-shear alerts
yanilgi: The storm didn't look dangerous enough to avoid. Microbursts were poorly understood and hard to see.
tartisma: Detection technology followed the crash. How many hazards do we understand only after a disaster?
basliklar: Why Delta Flight 191 Crashed
The Microburst Pilots Couldn't See
sahneler: On approach to Dallas, a Lockheed TriStar slammed into the ground.
It hit cars and a water tank, and more than one hundred thirty people were killed.
It had flown beneath a thunderstorm.
A microburst was blasting down from the cloud.
First a headwind, then a downdraft, then a sudden tailwind.
The jet lost airspeed too close to the ground to recover.
Microbursts were barely understood then.
Airports and jets now carry wind-shear detection.

baslik: The Jet That Slid Off a Snowy Runway Into a Street
sonuc: slid off the runway into a Chicago street
tetik: a delayed use of thrust reversers on a snowy runway
mekanizma: runway overrun from contaminated runway, tailwind and late reverse thrust
ders: landing distance assessments and reverser procedures were revised
yanilgi: The brakes worked. The jet needed more stopping distance than the crew's calculation assumed.
tartisma: A child in a car outside the airport was killed. How much safety area should urban airports have?
basliklar: Why Southwest Flight 1248 Overran the Runway
The Snowy Landing That Ended in a Street
sahneler: In a snowstorm, a Boeing 737 slid off the end of a runway at Chicago Midway.
It crashed through a fence into a street, and a child in a car was killed.
The runway was covered in snow.
There was a tailwind component.
The thrust reversers were deployed late.
The jet needed more distance than it had.
Midway has little space beyond its runways.
Landing distance procedures were revised afterward.

baslik: The Spoilers That Weren't Armed for a Stormy Landing
sonuc: overran the runway at Little Rock in a storm
tetik: landing in a thunderstorm with spoilers not armed
mekanizma: overrun on a wet runway without spoilers deploying, reducing braking
ders: airlines stressed limits on landing in thunderstorms and checklist completion
yanilgi: The storm alone didn't cause the overrun. Without spoilers, the wheels had far less grip.
tartisma: The crew pushed to land before the weather worsened. How does time pressure change decisions?
basliklar: Why American Airlines Flight 1420 Overran the Runway
The Spoilers That Never Deployed
sahneler: Landing in a thunderstorm, an MD-82 ran off the runway at Little Rock.
It struck approach lights and broke apart, and eleven people died.
The crew had been rushing to land before the storm got worse.
They didn't arm the spoilers.
Spoilers dump lift and press the wheels onto the runway.
Without them, braking on the wet surface was poor.
The crew was also tired after a long day.
Airlines stressed thunderstorm limits and checklist completion.

baslik: Cargo Broke Loose and Crushed the Controls of a 747
sonuc: stalled and crashed just after take-off
tetik: armoured vehicles breaking free of their straps
mekanizma: shifting cargo damaging hydraulics and the horizontal stabilizer drive, causing an unrecoverable pitch-up
ders: cargo restraint procedures for heavy vehicles were overhauled
yanilgi: The engines and airframe were fine. Loose cargo destroyed the systems that control pitch.
tartisma: The restraint method wasn't in the approved manual. Who approves how unusual cargo is tied down?
basliklar: Why National Airlines Flight 102 Crashed
The Cargo That Broke Loose at Take-Off
sahneler: Seconds after take-off from Bagram, a Boeing 747 pitched up steeply.
It stalled and crashed, killing all seven crew.
It was carrying heavy armoured vehicles.
Their straps had not been secured correctly.
As the jet climbed, a vehicle broke loose and rolled backward.
It damaged hydraulics and the tail's control system.
The pilots could not lower the nose.
Cargo restraint procedures were overhauled afterward.

baslik: The Military Charter That Crashed Leaving Gander
sonuc: crashed shortly after take-off from Gander
tetik: a take-off with probable ice on the wings
mekanizma: probable wing ice contamination reducing lift, though the cause was disputed by investigators
ders: de-icing practices were scrutinized, and the disputed findings remain a case study
yanilgi: The official finding of ice was contested. Some board members argued for other causes.
tartisma: Investigators disagreed publicly. What happens when an investigation board splits?
basliklar: Why Arrow Air Flight 1285 Crashed
The Disputed Crash at Gander
sahneler: A chartered DC-8 carrying US soldiers crashed just after take-off in Newfoundland.
All two hundred fifty six people aboard were killed.
It had stopped at Gander to refuel in winter.
The aircraft was not de-iced.
The majority of investigators blamed ice on the wings.
Ice reduces lift and makes a heavy jet climb poorly.
Several board members disagreed and argued for other causes.
The split findings remain a case study in investigation.

baslik: The Ambiguous Clearance That Put a Jet Into a Mountain
sonuc: hit a mountain on approach to Washington Dulles
tetik: a clearance the crew read as permission to descend
mekanizma: premature descent in cloud due to ambiguous approach clearance and charts
ders: ground proximity warning systems became mandatory on US airliners
yanilgi: The pilots believed they were following the clearance. The wording didn't make the minimum altitude clear.
tartisma: Another airline had nearly done the same weeks earlier and reported it internally. Why wasn't it shared?
basliklar: Why TWA Flight 514 Hit a Mountain
The Clearance That Sounded Like Permission
sahneler: On approach to Washington Dulles, a Boeing 727 flew into a mountain.
Everyone aboard was killed, ninety two people.
The crew believed they were cleared to descend.
The clearance didn't make the safe altitude clear.
Cloud hid the terrain ahead.
The jet had no terrain warning system.
Weeks earlier, another crew had nearly done the same.
Ground proximity warnings then became mandatory.

baslik: An Engine Failure the Crew Made Worse
sonuc: crashed after an engine failed on take-off
tetik: an uncontained engine failure from a cracked spacer
mekanizma: engine failure followed by improper control inputs leading to a stall
ders: engine-failure training at take-off was emphasized
yanilgi: A twin jet can climb on one engine. The crash followed from how the failure was handled.
tartisma: Both a mechanical failure and a human response were involved. Where should the fix go first?
basliklar: Why Midwest Express Flight 105 Crashed
When an Engine Failure Became a Stall
hook: One engine should have been enough
soru: Fix the part or the training?
sahneler: Just after take-off from Milwaukee, a DC-9's engine failed.
Seconds later, the jet rolled and crashed, killing all thirty one aboard.
A cracked part inside the engine had broken apart.
A twin jet can climb on one engine.
But the crew's control inputs were wrong for the failure.
The jet slowed, rolled and stalled.
Both the engine and the response were investigated.
Training for engine failures at take-off was emphasized.

baslik: The Rocket Launch That Flew Four Inches
sonuc: rose a few inches and shut down
tetik: two umbilical plugs disconnecting in the wrong order
mekanizma: electrical sequencing fault from umbilical plugs of different lengths separating out of order
ders: ground umbilical design and electrical sequencing were changed
yanilgi: The rocket didn't explode. It sat back on the pad while its escape tower flew off on its own.
tartisma: A fully fuelled rocket then sat armed on the pad. How do you safe a rocket nobody can approach?
basliklar: The Mercury-Redstone Flight That Went Four Inches
The Plugs That Came Out in the Wrong Order
sahneler: An uncrewed Mercury rocket ignited on the pad and rose a few inches.
Then its engine suddenly shut down, and it settled back onto the pad.
The escape tower fired and flew off on its own.
The capsule's parachutes popped out.
Two electrical plugs had disconnected in the wrong order.
One was slightly longer than the other.
That sequence told the rocket to shut down.
Umbilical design and electrical sequencing were changed.

baslik: The Shuttle That Survived Heat-Shield Damage — Years Before Columbia
tetik: debris from a booster striking the orbiter at launch
mekanizma: launch debris removing and damaging thermal protection tiles
ders: the near-miss was later cited as a warning before Columbia
yanilgi: Luck mattered. The missing tile happened to sit over a thick metal antenna plate.
tartisma: The crew reported damage that mission managers downplayed. What did this mission teach that was forgotten?
basliklar: How STS-27 Nearly Became Columbia
The Heat-Shield Damage Atlantis Survived
sahneler: Space Shuttle Atlantis returned from a secret mission badly damaged.
Hundreds of heat-shield tiles had been hit, and one was gone, destroyed at launch.
Debris from a booster struck the orbiter during launch.
In orbit, the crew saw the damage on camera.
Mission managers judged it not serious.
The missing tile sat over a thick metal antenna plate.
That plate protected the structure during re-entry.
Years later, Columbia was lost to similar damage.

baslik: The Rocket Nose Cone That Wouldn't Open — Twice
ad: the Taurus XL launches of OCO and Glory
tetik: a payload fairing that did not separate
mekanizma: fairing separation failure leaving the rocket too heavy to reach orbit
ders: NASA moved later climate missions to other rockets
yanilgi: The satellite was fine. It never escaped the nose cone meant to protect it.
tartisma: The same failure destroyed a second satellite two years later. Why didn't the first fix work?
basliklar: Why the Orbiting Carbon Observatory Never Reached Orbit
The Fairing That Failed Twice
sahneler: A NASA satellite built to measure carbon dioxide never reached orbit.
Minutes after launch, it fell into the ocean.
The rocket's nose cone didn't separate.
Carrying its extra weight, the rocket couldn't reach orbit.
Engineers worked on a fix.
Two years later, another NASA satellite was lost the same way.
Both flew on the same type of rocket.
NASA moved later missions to other launchers.
